claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK

  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is fostered but the council is not paying for accommodation or maintenance
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to know about the children you're claiming Child Benefit for.

**How old is your child (or the oldest child if you have more than one)?**

Please let me know:
- Your child's age (or ages if you have multiple children)
- Their names (so I can track them through the assessment)

This will help me guide you through the right eligibility checks. The age of your child determines which rules apply to your claim.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 15 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thanks for that information. So you have **Alex, who is 15 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, this is great news - children under 16 automatically qualify as "qualifying children" for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few other important eligibility requirements for you as the person claiming.

Let me move forward with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

This is to check that Alex meets the work requirements for eligibility. Since Alex is 15, this is likely a straightforward yes, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - just focuses on school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's perfect. Alex doesn't work, so this requirement is met.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, we need to check whether Alex is receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit (in their own name/right)

As a 15-year-old in school, this would be unlikely, but I need to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't get any benefits in their own name - nothing like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex doesn't receive those benefits.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since Alex is 15 and in school, I expect the answer is no. But let me confirm:
- Is Alex currently in any type of apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship - just regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in regular school, not an apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status, as this is an important eligibility requirement for Child Benefit.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

I also need to check if any of these special circumstances apply to you:
- Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?
- Do you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (and are working, job-seeking, studying, or have sufficient resources)?
- Are you a Crown servant living abroad?

For most people, the answer to the first question will determine eligibility. Can you tell me where you normally live?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, so you meet the residency requirements.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. This is about whether you're the person responsible for Alex's care and upkeep.

**Do you live with Alex, or are you responsible for contributing to Alex's upkeep?**

Responsibility for a child means either:
- You live with the child, OR
- You contribute to their upkeep (e.g., paying for food, clothes, housing, pocket money, presents, etc.) - the contribution should be at least equivalent to the Child Benefit amount, OR
- You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you clearly have responsibility for them.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check if anyone else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or if there's any other person who might be claiming.

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent) claiming for Alex?

Or is it just you claiming?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming for Alex - it's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So there's no other claimant for Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now let me check where Alex is living at the moment.

**Is Alex in any of these situations?**
- In hospital?
- In residential care?
- Fostered?
- Or living with you at home normally?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, I'm actually fostering Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that - that's an important detail. So Alex is in a fostering arrangement with you.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
This is an important question for fostered children:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for Alex's accommodation and upkeep yourself, or is the council covering these costs as part of the fostering arrangement?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't get anything from the council for fostering Alex - I'm covering everything myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! So you're covering all of Alex's accommodation and maintenance costs yourself, with no council payments.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Wonderful! Based on all the information you've provided, I can now confirm your eligibility status. Let me record the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You Are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

**Great news!** You can claim Child Benefit for **Alex**.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

✅ **Alex meets all qualifying requirements:**
- Age 15 (under 16 - automatic qualifying age)
- Not working full-time
- Not receiving benefits in their own right
- Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

✅ **You meet all claimant requirements:**
- You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- You live with Alex and are responsible for their care
- You're covering all of Alex's accommodation and maintenance costs yourself
- No one else is claiming for Alex

✅ **Special circumstances handled:**
- Even though Alex is a foster child, because you're not receiving any council payments toward their care, you are eligible to claim Child Benefit

### Next Steps:

1. **Make your claim** through the UK government website at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit
2. **Gather documents** you might need:
   - Proof of your identity
   - Proof of Alex's identity and age
   - Details about the fostering arrangement
3. **Backdate your claim** if needed (claims can usually be backdated up to 3 months)

If you have any questions or your circumstances change, you can contact HMRC's Child Benefit office or update your claim online.

Congratulations, and best of luck with your claim!

Although Alex is in a fostering arrangement, you are covering all of Alex's accommodation and maintenance costs yourself without any council payments, which means you can claim Child Benefit for Alex.
